records.name: Surge Recovery
records.summary: A recovery house network for men in Philadelphia who are working through alcohol and drug addiction. Residents live on site for a 90-day stay and can take job training, GED and college prep classes, and outpatient therapy.
records.what_you_do: Live in the residential program, take the classes and job training it offers, and use its health and outpatient services. Alumni can stay connected through the program's alumni services.

schedule.text: Residential program with a 90-day stay. Office hours Monday to Thursday, 10 am to 6 pm, and Friday, 10 am to 3 pm. Education classes run twice a week, three hours each time.

first_step.how: Call the office on a weekday between 10 am and 6 pm to ask about the intake process
first_step.basis: Admission is limited to men over 18 and starts with an intake step, so there is no simple walk in.

records.notes: Residential recovery program, not a peer support group, so the support-recovery family was not used. The site lists three phone numbers (215-471-3570, 215-417-3570, 215-468-4017) and does not say which is current, so the phone is left blank until verified. The IRS street address 644 S 60th St, 19143 is not shown on the site, so no location is recorded. Site shows no dated items; its 2026 copyright is not used as evidence.

records.name: The Pennsylvania Post
records.summary: A student newspaper that reports on the University of Pennsylvania campus, with sections for news, opinion, arts, sports, data, and podcasts. Students can write, edit, or design for it.
records.what_you_do: Write stories, columns, or reviews, or join an editing or design team. The site lists open editor spots for data, copy, and layout and design.

first_step.how: Email thepennsylvaniapost@gmail.com to say you want to join; the site says the paper is still recruiting
first_step.basis: The site gives a clear email and says the paper is recruiting, though it does not describe meeting times or a sign-up process.

records.notes: Student-run newspaper, not a community group, but students can join and it is a real, active student organization in University City. Only students are the intended audience. Newest dated item on the homepage is a May 21, 2026 column. Meeting times and address are not on the site; the IRS address 4053 Spruce St, 19104 is not used.

records.name: Workers Revolutionary Collective
records.summary: A cooperative of member-run collectives in Philadelphia that does mutual aid. Its projects include food and land work, a laundry for people without stable housing, a car-share network, and worker education and media.
records.what_you_do: Pick a collective that fits your skills, such as land care, media and economic education, art, or the laundry and mutual aid work, and reach out through the site.

cost.text: Participation cost not stated; the site asks for optional donations

first_step.how: Fill out the Worker Introduction form on wrc.life, then say which collective interests you
first_step.basis: The site has a public intake form and a contact page, but no meeting schedule or membership steps.

records.notes: OWNER REVIEW: the group calls itself openly political and anti-capitalist. The page does not mention candidates, parties, or elections, so it was kept under the nonpartisan rule, but please decide. Legal name Workers Revolutionary Collective Inc. No dated events or news on the page, and no phone or email is shown. Donation methods on the site were not recorded.

records.name: YEAH Philly
records.summary: A Black-led nonprofit that works with young people ages 15 to 24 in West and Southwest Philadelphia. It supports youth affected by violence and runs a weekday hangout, violence prevention work, and youth volunteer and work openings.
records.what_you_do: Stop by the hangout on a weekday afternoon or evening, or ask about volunteer and work openings. The group also publishes news and videos about youth issues.

schedule.text: Hangout open Monday to Friday, 2 to 10 pm. Saturdays are for scheduled events only. Closed Sunday. Ages 15 to 24.

first_step.how: Walk in to the hangout at 5257 Walton Ave on a weekday between 2 and 10 pm, or email teens@yeahphilly.org to ask about volunteer or work openings
first_step.basis: The site posts hangout hours and a street address, which suggests drop in is fine; it lists no sign-up steps for new visitors, so confirm by phone or email.

records.notes: Legal name: Youth Empowerment for Advancement Hangout. The site shows a 2025 copyright and a 2024 annual report link, which are not used as dates. Newest dated item is a news page entry from January 27, 2025. The calendar of events is linked but showed no listed dates when checked. Ages 15 to 24 are from the site's own description.

records.name: Luv-N-Bunns Rabbit Rescue
records.summary: A rabbit rescue that takes in domestic rabbits from shelters, strays, and hoarding cases and places them in foster and adoptive homes in the Philadelphia area. It also arranges veterinary care and holds rabbit care outreach events.
records.what_you_do: Foster a rabbit until it is adopted, volunteer through the application on the site, or adopt after an emailed application and screening.

schedule.text: Adoptions usually happen at a weekend adoption day after an approved application. No dates are posted on the site.

cost.text: Adoption fee not stated on the site

first_step.how: Email bunnies@luvnbunns.org to ask for an adoption application, or use the volunteer application linked from the site
first_step.basis: Adoption and volunteering both start with an application that is screened before you can meet the animals or start.

records.notes: Adoption counters on the site read 0, and the adoptables page showed no rabbit listings when checked, so the site may be stale or the page did not fully load. Status comes from a working site with no dates, and the 2026 label is not used as evidence. The site gives no phone or street address. A 2022 foster guide file name is not used as a date.

records.name: NE Phila Connected
records.summary: A neighborhood group in Northeast Philadelphia that runs a town watch and helps residents, including immigrant and limited-English speakers, find local resources. It also holds information meetings on local programs and laws.
records.what_you_do: Take part in the town watch, come to an information meeting, or ask for help connecting with local services.

first_step.how: Call (844) 533-3362 to ask about the next town watch or information meeting
first_step.basis: A public phone number and a stated focus on welcoming residents, though the site posts no meeting schedule.

records.notes: The site shows zero impact counters, has some typos, and has no dated content, so activity is uncertain. The /news page returned 404 when checked. Legal name NE Phila Connected. The IRS address 605 Lawler St, 19116 is not shown on the site, so no location is recorded. The Facebook group was listed as a link only and was not read.

records.name: ATTRACT Philly
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit for young people that runs mentoring and leadership programs, including literacy, mock job interviews, and a scholarship. It also runs service events such as a toy drive and a movie night.
records.what_you_do: Join a signature program such as Born to Lead, Literacy for Leaders, or Queen's Code, take part in a service event, or ask about volunteering or an internship.

first_step.how: Fill out the Become a Volunteer page on the site, or email attract.philly@gmail.com to ask about the next program
first_step.basis: Volunteer sign-up and a Request Program page are public, but program ages, dates, and sign-up steps are not posted.

records.notes: Newest dated items are a May 7, 2025 scholarship announcement and a June 30, 2025 scholarship deadline. The footer reads 2018 and the header has a placeholder phone link, which is not used. The mailing address is a P.O. Box in Philadelphia 19118; the IRS street address 6009 N 13th St, 19141 is not shown on the site. Program ages are not stated. The header also lists info@attractphilly.org, which was not recorded.

records.name: Bringing Everybody Together
records.summary: A community group for young people that runs programs such as an after school program, a chess program, and a youth-led online talk show.
records.what_you_do: Join an after school or chess program, or take part in the youth-led talk show. Use the contact form to ask which program fits and how to sign up.

first_step.how: Use the Contact Us form on mybetfamily.com to ask which youth program is running and how to sign up
first_step.basis: The site lists programs but gives no dates, times, or sign-up steps, and the only contact route is a form.

records.notes: The site name is MyBetFamily; this record uses the everyday name from the IRS list. The homepage lists program names but no dates, times, or contact details other than a form. A 2026 footer is not used as evidence. The site mentions social media by handle only, with no platform link, so none was recorded. The IRS address 4809 N 18th St, 19141 is not shown on the site, so no location is recorded. Program ages are not stated.
